name: Art Deco Jewellery
summary: Hard, bright geometry in platinum. The stones are diamonds in baguette and square cuts, black onyx, rock crystal and carved coloured stones, set in strips, fans and sunbursts. It was shown at Paris in 1925.

philosophy.core_thesis: A jewel is a machine-age design: a hard, flat pattern of line, angle and contrast in white metal and stones.
design_principles: Build the design from straight lines, circles and angles, in a symmetrical pattern.
Contrast white and black: diamonds and platinum beside black onyx or black enamel.
Cut stones in sharp shapes: baguette, square, triangle and calibre, and set them flat in rows.
Use platinum or white gold for the frame, with the claws hidden and the lines as thin as a thread.
Add one strong colour in a carved stone: emerald, ruby or sapphire carved as a leaf, a fruit or a flower (the Tutti Frutti style).
Take forms from the machine, from Egypt, from India and from Cubism: a fan, a sunburst, a stepped skyline.
Make the piece as a strip, a clip or a bracelet that moves, with a flat front and a hinge.
Set stones with no visible metal, in the mystery setting, so that the stones look like one surface.
anti_patterns: Soft pastel enamel and wire tendrils

silhouette.shape: A flat, geometric jewel: a strap bracelet, a double clip brooch, a long drop earring or a ring with a large central stone.
silhouette.line: Straight and symmetrical, in steps, fans and circles, with sharp corners.
silhouette.fit: A strap bracelet lies flat on the wrist, a clip sits on the dress at the hip, a long earring hangs below the bobbed hair.
silhouette.proportion: A strap bracelet is 2 to 4 cm wide. A double clip is 6 to 8 cm wide. A long drop earring is 5 to 8 cm long.
rules: Set baguette diamonds in rows of three, five or seven, with a black onyx band between them.
Fit a strap bracelet from many flat links that lie close to the wrist.
Wear a long earring with a geometric drop over a bobbed haircut.
Pin a double clip at the hip or the lapel, and join the two halves as a brooch.

fabrics.rule: Use platinum for the frame, and set white stones against black onyx or black enamel, with one carved colour as an accent.

methods: baguette and calibre cut stones in rows
mystery setting with no visible metal
carved emerald, ruby and sapphire leaves
construction.closures: A hidden box clasp on a bracelet and a collar; a double-pin clip on a brooch; a clip or a post on an earring.
construction.details: Stepped edges, fan and sunburst shapes, a black band, a carved coloured stone and a flat, polished face.

surface.pattern: Geometric rows, fans, steps and sunbursts; a flat front with sharp edges.
surface.gloss: Very high: platinum and diamond at 90 to 100 GU, set against matte black onyx or enamel.
surface.wear: Platinum keeps its colour; onyx and enamel chip at the edge, and the mystery setting is hard to repair.

palette.strategy: Black and white as the base, with one strong jewel colour in a carved stone.

processes: stone carving of leaves and fruit
making.scale: The Paris houses and a few New York houses; each piece by a team of makers over weeks, in a small run.
making.signs: Sharp geometry, symmetrical layout, flat polished surface, a black and white contrast and a hinged strap.

Double clip brooch in geometric steps

Sautoir of onyx beads with a diamond tassel

positive: platinum and baguette diamond strap bracelet
long drop earrings with bobbed hair

canonical_works.work: Jewels shown at the Exposition Internationale

evidence.title: Art Deco bracelet (1925) Museum of Decorative Arts
Art Deco style jewelry, 1915-1930, designed by Paul Flato

emotion.target_response: A hard, bright and confident glitter: the viewer sees speed, order and wealth in a clean pattern.

use_cases: costume design for a 1920s or 1930s drama
a luxury jewellery brief with a graphic look
a museum label for an Exposition piece
an image prompt for a Jazz Age jewel
avoid_when: the brief wants flowing curves or hand-made silver
the brief wants a soft, romantic look

modifiers.how: Swap platinum for yellow and rose gold, round the corners into curls and bows, and enlarge the coloured stones.
Swap platinum and diamonds for chrome, paste and Bakelite, and keep the geometry and the black and white contrast.

ornament_level.note: The geometry gives the ornament; a plain strap sits at the low end.
